neighbours.label: Inner piece of a narrative body-movement verb that the tokenizer splits (cl|ut|ched, gr|app|led, trem|bled): weak, broad pole
fire: Halfway down the icy steps, Nora clutched her brother's sleeve.
On the dark landing the boy shuddered and backed toward the wall.
The puppy wriggled out of my arms and ran into the garden.
Lying in the tent, she squirmed inside her damp sleeping bag.
The old man's lips quivered as he read the letter again.
In the ring the two wrestlers grappled for almost a minute.
As the thunder rolled closer, the horse flinched at every flash.
Under the bridge the stranger writhed in pain until help came.
quiet: Halfway down the icy steps, Nora grabbed her brother's sleeve.
On the dark landing the boy stopped and backed toward the wall.
The puppy jumped out of my arms and ran into the garden.
Lying in the tent, she slept inside her damp sleeping bag.
The old man's voice rose as he read the letter again.
In the ring the two wrestlers fought for almost a minute.
As the thunder rolled closer, the horse shook at every flash.
Under the bridge the stranger waited in pain until help came.

predictions: Split physical-reaction verbs (clutched, grappled, trembled, shuddered, wriggled) reach 0.3-0.8; the same sentence with a single-token verb (grabbed, shook, held) stays under 0.15.
